scenes.title: The problem
scenes.purpose: Establish uncertainty as the problem, without blaming the operator or implying a physical TARK field trial.
scenes.narration: Out here, fog does more than hide the road. It changes what a driver can trust. Is that shape a vehicle, a person, or the edge of the road? We started with that uncertainty. Our challenge wasn't simply to see farther. It was to know when the evidence was no longer good enough.
scenes.visual: Retain the mine concept and restrained push. Use a short question, not a definition. Keep the original blue guide brief.
scenes.camera: Very slow forward push from a wide establishing frame; hold the silhouette's scale, with no dramatic chase.
scenes.animation: A near object remains discernible while the distant outline softens. Animate a single visibility boundary without distance numbers. The guide looks to the question, then exits.
scenes.sound: Original low atmospheric pad; soft synthesized wind and restrained distant industrial ambience. Pause after the first sentence.
scenes.transition: Fog dissolves into the neutral studio background of the conceptual prototype.
scenes.accuracy: Not mine footage, not a completed TARK vehicle, and not a fog-performance demonstration. Do not add a simulated pedestrian detection box or invented detection range.

scenes.title: TARK reveal
scenes.purpose: Introduce TARK and distinguish its conceptual physical build from the current software baseline.
scenes.narration: So we built TARK around a question: when visibility drops, how do we make a more informed decision? Let us show you. This engineering demonstrator brings sensing interfaces, reasoning, bounded control, and monitoring together. You're seeing conceptual hardware alongside our integrated software demonstration, not a claim of completed mine testing.
scenes.visual: Retain the rover reveal. Replace the repeated pending badge with a clear SOFTWARE DEMONSTRATOR scope label and complementary integration callouts.
scenes.camera: Slow lateral studio reveal; a modest parallax push rather than a false fully modelled orbit when using a still asset.
scenes.animation: Sequential three-item callout groups. Preserve four wheels and two geared-motor assemblies; leave unverified mechanical transmission details abstract. No physical cable-routing detail or fabricated module pinout.
scenes.sound: Add a quiet regular pulse under the atmosphere; warm, conversational narration.
scenes.transition: A sensor callout grows into the three-column sensing view.
scenes.accuracy: All physical imagery is conceptual. Protected regulated 5 V logic is a planned power rail, not an instruction to feed every breakout 5 V. Do not imply components are physically assembled.

scenes.title: Complementary evidence
scenes.purpose: Explain complementary sensor roles while making the actual runtime decision boundary explicit.
scenes.narration: Different sensors answer different questions. Radar provides local targets. Cameras add visual context; thermal sensing adds temperature patterns. The inertial sensor describes orientation. Encoders report wheel response, not ground speed. Today, radar feeds our decision pipeline. Other sensors supply observations and health information.
scenes.visual: Retain sensor-role graphics. Reveal each observation card when its role is spoken. Explicitly separate the radar decision input from the observation interfaces without a large negative fusion banner.
scenes.camera: Controlled macro-style push toward each sensor tile; return to a stable three-lane layout.
scenes.animation: Only the radar observation lane joins the current decision pipeline. Camera, thermal, and IMU lanes end at health/observation panels. Encoder arrows connect to wheel-response context, not a ground-speed label. No merged fusion blob.
scenes.sound: One soft original electronic pulse as each distinct data role appears; no fabricated sensor recording.
scenes.transition: Follow the radar lane into the Pi health and freshness blocks.
scenes.accuracy: RGB/thermal/IMU are observation-only in the current runtime, not completed perception fusion. Do not show measured temperatures, imagery, pulse rates, or a physically connected sensor without actual evidence.

scenes.title: Pi reasoning
scenes.purpose: Show why freshness, health, tracking, and uncertainty precede an operational decision.
scenes.narration: Inside the Raspberry Pi, we ask something before trusting a reading: is it healthy, fresh, and worth using? Then we follow radar targets over time, rather than treating every detection as a new object. Uncertainty travels with that track. If an observation gets old, the system shouldn't quietly present yesterday's confidence as today's evidence.
scenes.visual: Retain the Pi evidence path. Highlight health, tracking and uncertainty to actual spoken timing; stale readings branch away from evidence.
scenes.camera: Gentle dolly into the compute block, then a stable top-down technical view.
scenes.animation: An explicitly ILLUSTRATIVE fresh token advances while a stale token diverts to an unavailable/uncertain side lane. Outline width represents uncertainty qualitatively, not a claimed probability. Use no invented target coordinates or timing thresholds.
scenes.sound: Soft regular processing pulse; reduce the bed briefly at 'not automatically evidence'.
scenes.transition: An uncertainty outline becomes the qualitative stopping-distance graphic.
scenes.accuracy: Animation explains software responsibilities; it is not a recording of a packet-level execution. Do not imply every optional sensor contributes to the radar decision path. No universal claim that all stale values are physically rejected at hardware.

scenes.title: Time and stopping
scenes.purpose: Explain TTC and stopping-distance concepts without claiming currently unimplemented runtime TTC use or measured braking.
scenes.narration: Now, seeing something isn't the same as having enough room to respond. Time to collision asks how quickly a closing situation could develop. In this demo, you'll see that value marked unavailable. Stopping requirement brings together reaction distance, braking distance, and margin. Comparing that requirement with observable distance gives us the next question: what operation can the evidence justify?
scenes.visual: Separate TTC concept from current runtime; retain N/A visibly. Build the stopping comparison as reaction, braking and margin are spoken. Keep parameterized, not measured, scope concise.
scenes.camera: Slow top-down tracking of the qualitative distance bars, then a slight pullback revealing the separate TTC helper.
scenes.animation: TTC helper remains visually disconnected from the current PV-SOE arrow. Build the stopping requirement as three labelled segments; a separate observable-distance bar is compared with it. Avoid any precise length ratio presented as data.
scenes.sound: Music becomes simpler; one restrained accent when the two distance concepts separate.
scenes.transition: The comparison frame contracts into an operating-envelope outline.
scenes.accuracy: TTC helper exists but current snapshot TTC is unavailable and does not drive today's decision. Observable distance is compared with stopping requirement, not inserted as a braking-performance measurement. Reaction/deceleration/margin parameters are provisional and not physically validated.

scenes.title: Operating envelope
scenes.purpose: Explain PV-SOE and conservative state reporting while making permanent Phase 1 zero-output authority unmistakable.
scenes.narration: We call that the Perception-Verified Safe Operating Envelope. The idea is simple: weaker evidence should mean less operating freedom, not more guesswork. NORMAL, RESTRICT, STOP, and UNKNOWN make that judgement visible. UNKNOWN is important. It says we don't have enough trustworthy information. A missing sensor or stale message must never quietly create permission to do more.
scenes.visual: Retain the qualitative envelope and four implemented runtime states. Highlight each state with the spoken name. Keep simulation outputs zero in a compact factual strip rather than narrating a phase-status warning.
scenes.camera: Stable medium technical composition with one restrained push into the zero-output strip.
scenes.animation: Qualitative envelope shrinks as uncertainty rises. States highlight as conceptual alternatives, not a claimed live trace. No vehicle motion. Keep the phase strip fixed across every state.
scenes.sound: Quiet pulse, with less music on the zero-output statement; no warning siren.
scenes.transition: The fixed zero-command strip moves into the Pi-to-controller lane.
scenes.accuracy: Do not animate NORMAL -> WARN -> RESTRICT -> STOP as implemented behavior. WARN exists in the wider vocabulary but is not emitted by the current decision path. A NORMAL software state does not authorize traction; DISABLED_PHASE_1 remains absolute.

scenes.title: Separate authority
scenes.purpose: Separate bounded software control, planned independent physical isolation, and browser observation.
scenes.narration: The Pi handles reasoning. The ESP thirty-two software checks bounded commands before accepting them. Separately, our electrical design gives the emergency stop an independent path through the contactor system. Those responsibilities stay separate. And the dashboard never controls the vehicle. In this software demonstration, traction stays disabled; neither a browser click nor a healthy-looking screen grants motion authority.
scenes.visual: Retain three architecture lanes. Synchronize local control, physical isolation design and monitoring with narration. Black dashed mechanical relationship remains distinct. No demonstrated physical operation claim.
scenes.camera: Stable schematic top-down view; gently emphasize one lane at a time. No orbit around terminal diagrams.
scenes.animation: COBS, CRC32C, and CBOR appear as sequential software-envelope checks, followed by response arrows back to Pi. Main and auxiliary K1 meanings stay separate. Physical mechanism link is black dashed, never an electrical junction. Do not animate a physical motor turning or claim a contactor test.
scenes.sound: Restrained electronic acknowledgement for software; a clearly illustrative soft contact click may mark the planned isolation concept, not a recorded successful test.
scenes.transition: Observation lane carries the viewer toward the geographic map context.
scenes.accuracy: Pi remains decision authority and ESP32 a bounded validation layer. Board-specific USB/watchdog binding and physical verification are pending. The physical NC E-stop path is designed independently but unresolved electrical HOLDs must be cleared before energization. Never connect browser directly to motors.

scenes.title: Location context
scenes.purpose: Separate GNSS geographic observation from radar-local coordinates and show honest no-fix behavior.
scenes.narration: Location answers another question: where are we on the map? That's the role of GNSS and the intended LC twenty-nine H receiver. But radar asks where a target is relative to our vehicle. We keep those coordinate systems separate. Without a vehicle fix, the map uses a clearly labelled India overview, not an invented location.
scenes.visual: Retain the actual simulated map and clearly separated radar-local coordinate inset. Geographic context never becomes motion authority.
scenes.camera: Gentle crop into the real Map capture, then a small pullback to reveal the separate XY inset.
scenes.animation: Highlight geographic coordinate labels and local XY axes sequentially. Never manufacture satellite acquisition, an actual fix, or location values. Do not replace the application's real source labels.
scenes.sound: Light original transition sweep; calm narrator, no GPS-lock chime.
scenes.transition: Match the real map application's navigation/header into the dashboard capture.
scenes.accuracy: GNSS is observational and cannot command motors. Do not mix browser location with vehicle location. A displayed public map is not evidence of a physically connected LC29H(AA), positional accuracy, or mine navigation.

scenes.title: Real dashboard
scenes.purpose: Show real current software evidence and the monitoring-only authority boundary.
scenes.narration: And this is the actual TARK dashboard. You're looking at our public software demo. The simulation labels stay visible. You can inspect system state, sensor health, communication, maps, logs, and replay. When a sensor is missing, the interface says so. For us, the important part is being able to ask why a decision happened, and trace the evidence behind it.
scenes.visual: Use genuine public UI stills, never relabel data. Let narrative mentions guide Sensors, Safety, Map, Logs and Replay presentation. Keep simulation and unavailable states legible.
scenes.camera: Small controlled crops within real screenshots or recordings; no crop may hide SIMULATION, NOT CONNECTED, stale, or traction-disabled context. Prefer legibility over cinematic zoom.
scenes.animation: Overlay at most one short editorial label at a time outside critical UI values. Real UI states are unaltered. Captured values are snapshots, not a live video feed unless an actual recording is available.
scenes.sound: A lighter modern pulse, with very soft original click accents on real navigation cuts. Do not imply telemetry sounds are hardware feedback.
scenes.transition: The dashboard frame scales down beside the documented software-baseline evidence.
scenes.accuracy: The public service is a software simulation/monitoring demonstration, not physical verification. Retain TTC N/A and actual unavailable sensor states. Only show pages that load in the actual deployment. If unavailable, request current captures instead of fabricating them.

scenes.title: Conclusion
scenes.purpose: Close with defensible software maturity, a concrete validation path, and the project's human-centered principle.
scenes.narration: We've brought sensing interfaces, reasoning, safety logic, and bounded control together with a real dashboard. One testable software system, not a collection of parts. The goal was never blind trust in a sensor. Trust the evidence you can verify. That's TARK.
scenes.visual: Replace the old unfinished-project comparison with a confident integration composition. Return to the existing conceptual rover and brief blue guide. End on TARK and the evidence principle, with a two-second locked title hold.
scenes.camera: Slow pullback to the conceptual platform, then a locked final title composition with a quiet two-second hold.
scenes.animation: Software and physical stages remain separate. No checkmark on physical verification, E-stop, mine field testing, or production readiness. Fade imagery down as the final principle resolves.
scenes.sound: Warm original harmonic resolution; fade music and ambience gently through the last two seconds. Leave the last title hold without narration.
scenes.transition: End on the held title, no outgoing fade, with the last two seconds clear of speech.
scenes.accuracy: Software evidence is a frozen tested baseline, not a guarantee of no defects or completed physical safety validation. Electrical DESIGN HOLDs remain. Do not claim mine certification, collision reduction, braking distance, fog range, or field reliability.
